title: Compact SDK OSS modules and deprecate legacy IO fields
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a coordinated dependency bump and surface-cleanup across the Python, JS, and Go SDKs. Goals: reduce transitive bloat by consolidating low-level IO/transport utilities into a single compact internal module, remove legacy request/response IO fields (legacy_input_stream, legacy_output_stream, optional_binary_payload) from public client APIs, and publish migration guidance. This reduces maintainability and minimizes duplicate code paths that are complicating kernel/runtime changes on the platform side.
acceptance_criteria: All three language clients (python, javascript, go) have upgrades that pin/align commonly shared dependencies to supported minor versions (requests/httpx for python, node-fetch/undici for js, net/http adapters for go)

A compact internal module is created in each repo (e.g., _io_compat) and client public surfaces no longer expose legacy_* IO fields; those fields are behind a shim flagged deprecated for one release and removed after migration window
End-to-end test matrix (unit + integration + perf) passes in CI for pinned deps and compact modules
Migration guide and upgrade notes published in SDK CHANGELOGs and README with code examples for migrating away from legacy_* fields
No customer-facing regressions in smoke tests; canary rollout on runtime 1.21 without increased tail latency or error rates
plan: Inventory current transitive deps and API fields across python/js/go SDKs
Design compact internal IO compatibility module for each language and add compatibility shims that map legacy fields to new primitives
Implement dep bumps and refactor imports to use compact modules
Add deprecation warnings in runtime when legacy fields are used
Run CI matrix and microbenchmarks to measure allocations and latency changes
Prepare migration docs, changelogs, and SDK release notes
Coordinate staged rollout: alpha -> canary -> GA with monitoring and rollback playbook
